title: The neighbor
hookLine: Jibril kept urging kindness to the neighbor until the Prophet ﷺ thought neighbors would inherit (Bukhari)
tomorrow: Removing a stone from the road
last: SADAQAH JARIYAH — THE WELL KEEPS GIVING.

cards: Quick question: what's the name of the person who lives closest to you? Not your closest friend. The closest person: the other side of your wall, across the hall, next door.
A lot of people don't know. They know strangers across the world by their usernames, and nod at the person ten feet away without ever learning a name.
They send money to causes overseas, which is good, and have never knocked on the door beside theirs. In Islam, charity has a starting point, and it's on the other side of your wall.

teach.b: Bukhari and Muslim report the Prophet ﷺ saying: Jibril kept urging me to be good to the neighbor, so much that I thought he would make the neighbor an heir.
An heir: someone with a legal share in what you leave behind, like family. That's how often the angel came back to it.

The Qur'an names neighbors in Surah an-Nisa, in a list of those to be good to: parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is related to you and the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side.

teach.h: BY ALLAH, HE DOES NOT BELIEVE.
teach.b: And Bukhari reports a warning so strong the Prophet said it three times: by Allah, he does not believe. Who? The one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm.
Sahih Muslim reports him telling the companion Abu Dharr: when you make a stew, add extra water, and look to your neighbors. Stretch the pot.
Bukhari reports him telling women not to think any gift to a neighbor too small, even a sheep's hoof. And a neighbor isn't defined by faith.

teach.h: HAVE YOU GIVEN TO OUR JEWISH NEIGHBOR?
teach.b: Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud report that the companion Abdullah ibn Amr had a sheep slaughtered, and when he came home the first thing he asked was: have you given some to our Jewish neighbor?
He had heard the Prophet's words about Jibril and the neighbor. Scholars have argued over how far a neighborhood stretches. The principle is simpler than any measuring.
Before the world, the house next door. Before the cause, the name.

how: Muslims give special weight to neighbors, of any faith: sharing food, visiting, helping and avoiding any harm to them, following the hadith of Jibril and the neighbor.

o: a pen pal you write to in another country
anyone nearby, of any faith, with real rights
a fellow Muslim who prays at your mosque

games.q: what's inside the neighbor — tap the pairs.
p: urged kindness until an heir seemed near
add water, look to your neighbors

s: in the hadith, only Muslim neighbors count
Abdullah ibn Amr asked first whether the Jewish neighbor had been given some (Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud).
the Prophet ﷺ swore three times about the one whose neighbor isn't safe from him
by Allah, he does not believe (Bukhari).
a small gift to a neighbor isn't worth giving
don't think any gift too small, even a sheep's hoof (Bukhari).

games.q: you're making a pot of stew, just enough for your family. the Prophet ﷺ has a word for Abu Dharr about it. what is it?
o: add extra water, and look to your neighbors
games.why: when you make a stew, add water and look to your neighbors (Muslim). stretch the pot.

practice: Picture the doors nearest yours, one by one, and notice which neighbors you know and which you don't.

Pick one, and picture something small you could bring: extra from dinner, a few pieces of fruit, a note with your name and number, even just a hello, since no gift is too small, not even a sheep's hoof.
Picture knocking, and their face, and if it makes you nervous, breathe through it.

wordCard.voice: The neighbor. The one next door, whose rights Jibril urged so often the Prophet thought they would inherit. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: start next door. Jibril kept coming back to the neighbor. That's day one hundred fifty-four.
